summary: @factiii/runner 0.28.0: static keyword co-occurrence in bundled CLI and embedder script, no traced installer-harm behavior
details: Static pattern matches fired on keyword co-occurrence inside a bundled dist/cli.js (multiple POST tokens across a large minified file) and on embedder/serve.py (ping/POST/GET tokens on nearby lines). The matches reflect that HTTP primitives appear somewhere in the bundle and that an embedding server script performs HTTP operations — common shapes for CLIs that talk to a service and for Python HTTP service wrappers. No specific installer-side data read is tied to a non-first-party destination, no lifecycle hook fetch-and-execute is present, no credential-path reads (~/.aws, ~/.ssh, ~/.npmrc, browser or wallet stores) are indicated, and no hardcoded attacker C2 is named. The evidence available is keyword proximity in bundled/minified code without a traced data-to-destination flow.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
